claims.text: Integrating high-throughput DSC with calibrated CALPHAD modeling can accurately and efficiently determine melting properties across a wide range of high-entropy alloys.
DSC can be used to determine melting temperature.
The DSC endothermic peaks observed for the HEAs correspond to melting.
Fusion enthalpy can be extracted from the DSC heat-flow profiles.
Fusion entropy can be deduced from the measured melting temperature and fusion enthalpy.
Dilatometry can detect the volume change of an HEA upon melting.
A CALPHAD database incorporating third-generation pure-element and Laves-phase models is suitable for interpreting HEA melting measurements.
CALPHAD modeling can model fusion thermodynamics and be compared with experimental fusion data.
The proposed CALPHAD calculations can predict liquid-phase heat capacities and densities for the HEAs.
Local chemical ordering or distortion in HEAs moderates the enthalpy change at melting.
Local chemical ordering or distortion in HEAs moderates the entropy change at melting.
The local chemical environment in HEAs influences liquid-phase density.
DSC and dilatometry indirectly capture the effects of the local chemical environment.
Joint experimental and computational analysis can resolve subtle thermodynamic contributions from chemical substitutions.
The HEA melting temperature will be determined with accuracy comparable to established reference materials and within typical DSC error bounds.
Measured fusion enthalpy, fusion entropy, and volume change will agree quantitatively with CALPHAD predictions within the expected uncertainty range.
The proposed performance applies to single-phase, as-cast HEAs with clear DSC signals and minimal phase separation or crucible interaction.
Phase changes, crucible reactions, and extreme compositional inhomogeneity can limit the approach.
CALPHAD prediction accuracy depends on the reliability of the underlying thermodynamic database.
High-temperature DSC baseline drift introduces uncertainty into the proposed measurements.

contradictions.description: The thermal range extends only slightly above the solidus, whereas determining total fusion enthalpy, entropy, volume change, and equilibrium liquid properties generally requires traversing the complete melting interval to at least the liquidus. The stated conditions may therefore not produce the fully molten state assumed by the mechanism and outcome.

The intervention describes CALPHAD as being calibrated and interpreted using the experimental data, while the validation design calls the CALPHAD calculation independent. Without a held-out calibration and validation split, these roles are not genuinely independent.
